title: Seven circuits around the House
note: The page's seven spiralling circuits of tawaf, the Black Stone corner marked as start and finish of every lap.

lines.text: Seven circuits, one direction, one corner
Makkah's House, the tenth of Dhul Hijjah
lines.sub: seven circuits return here every time

lines.text: Walk anticlockwise, the House on your left
Face the Black Stone and say Allahu akbar
Seven passes, counted from that corner
Lose count, and you build on the lower one

lines.sub: Hanafis: a duty, a sacrifice repairs it

lines.text: Tawaf is a pillar; nothing replaces it
The Black Stone marks the start and end
lines.sub: every circuit starts and ends there

research.retell: Tawaf is walking around the Kaaba seven times counterclockwise starting and ending at the Black Stone, and all four schools agree it is a pillar that nothing else can replace.
proof: Seven loops spiralling outward around a central cube, with the corner of the Black Stone marked as the start and the finish of every circuit.; with the House on your left
tawaf and sa’i return in the middle of the fifth day when you are tired... the tenth of Dhul Hijjah will be far easier
Tawaf is circling the Kaaba seven times, anticlockwise, with the House on your left. It starts at the corner of al-Hajar al-Aswad, the Black Stone, and it ends there.
face it, raise your right hand toward it and say Allahu akbar, and keep walking
Every circuit is one full pass from that corner back to it.; seven, counted from the Stone
Counting matters more than speed; lose count and you build on the lower number you are certain of.

Maliki, Shafi’i and Hanbali: purity ... is a condition of tawaf; a tawaf performed without wudu is not valid. Hanafi: purity is wajib, an obligation, not a condition; a tawaf performed without wudu is valid and a sacrifice repairs it.
Tawaf, seven circuits: Pillar, by agreement; Nothing replaces it. You remain in ihram until you perform it.
every circuit starts and ends here; Umrah, step by step
